benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_1: Simple nevus (benign nevus, pigmented nevus, mole, birthmark) – a benign neoplasm of the skin, which is a spot or a small nodule that rises slightly above the skin. Simple nevus can be either congenital or acquired (a characteristic appearance at any age). Approximately 3% of newborns have a plurality of simple nevi. With age, the proportion of multiplicity increases. By gender, simple nevi are somewhat more common in women compared with men, in a ratio of 3: 2, respectively.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of simple nevi. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor: the appearance of pigmented nevus may be due to the human genome
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_1_2: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet leads to faster reproduction of nevoid cells (nevus cells) and excessive production of melanin (pigment, the accumulation of which is noted in nevus)
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_1_3: Hormonal changes: hormonal fluctuations in the body (especially sex hormones, thyroid hormones and adrenal hormones) can affect the appearance of new nevi and the growth of existing ones;
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_1_4: Ionizing radiation, viral diseases and injuries can also trigger the appearance or growth of simple nevi.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of simple nevi is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_1: On visual inspection of a simple nevus, a spot or slightly elevated nodule is determined. Most often, the formation is symmetrical (oval or round), however, congenital nevi of large sizes can also be irregular in shape. The surface of the nevus is a texture of ordinary skin (rarely – slightly differs from the skin pattern).
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_2: The boundaries of benign nevus are clear and even. Large and giant congenital nevi can be with uneven edges. The color of simple nevus varies from tan to dark brown, with the distribution of pigment throughout the formation uniform. Sometimes there is a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery. The shades of the congenital nevus can change in the first years of a person’s life.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_3: The presence of benign nevus does not affect hair growth. Less often in the area of ​​congenital nevus there is a more intensive growth of coarse bristly hair, which is usually combined with pronounced brown pigmentation.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_4: The sizes of simple benign nevi can vary within wide limits, however, the most common formations are up to 10 mm. Nevi over 10 mm – in most cases congenital, they are rare, can reach 20 cm or more (giant congenital nevi).
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_5: On palpation of a simple nevus, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin. Subjective sensations are also absent.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_6: Neoplasms are located mainly on the trunk (~ 38%) or limbs (~ 48%), less often on the head and neck (~ 14%).
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_3_7: Nevi of the plantar and palmar surfaces (acral nevi) are somewhat different in shape, contour, and pigment distribution from ordinary nevi, which is associated with the presence of a characteristic skin pattern (“fingerprints”). Nevi of this localization are elongated in shape, have an uneven contour, darker color and pigment distribution in the form of parallel stripes.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of a simple nevus, the following features are visualized:
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_1: The pigment network is a pattern of hypopigmented holes and homogeneous lines from light brown to dark brown. The lines are evenly thinning to the periphery of the formation
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_2: Dots – are small hyperpigmented round structures that are located in the center or are found on the pigmented lines of the network
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_3: Globules – large hyperpigmented ring structures that are evenly distributed throughout the nevus or in the center, are rarely found on the periphery
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_4: Spots – hyperpigmented structureless areas located in the center
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_5: Vascular network – represented by slightly curved diffuse monomorphic vessels
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_6: Star radiance – pigmented stripes and dots located in the form of rays on the periphery
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_7: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_4_2: Acral nevi have some features in dermatoscopic imaging:
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_8: Accumulation of nevus cells is mainly found in furrows, and atypical melanocytes in ridges. The eccrine duct opens to the epidermis through ridges, which can help distinguish the ridge from the groove
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_4_9: The main pattern is trellised, parallel, and fibrillar. The fibrillar pattern is more common with the plantar surface of the foot (at the site of the greatest application of body weight)
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with pigmented neoplasms such as:
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_6_1: Simple nevus is safe and does not carry an increased risk of melanoma. In the absence of external effects on the pigmented nevus (trauma, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation) – the risk of malignant degeneration is comparable to the risk of melanoma on unchanged skin. Signs of a possible malignancy of a simple nevus: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_6_2: A slightly increased risk of melanoma is observed in congenital nevus, but this is more typical for large pigmented lesions (more than 20 cm in diameter). The risk of melanoma on the background of congenital nevus up to 20 cm is less than 1%.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_6_3: Large and multiple congenital nevi can be associated with various genetic syndromes and diseases, therefore, such patients require more careful observation and examination.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the simple nevus, changes in appearance and subjective sensations – self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the nevus has occurred, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications are made for removal of the damaged nevus. It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_7_4: Patients with congenital or multiple acquired moles require examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are also recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of pigmented nevus using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended.
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
benign_nevus.benign_nevus_desc_9_2: Also, a regular examination of the pigmented nevus, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms are necessary.

dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_1: Dermatofibroma – (skin fibroma, benign fibrous histiocytoma) benign neoplasm of the connective tissue genesis (non-melanocytic), represented by a knot, towering above the skin or intradermal dense knot. Dermatofibroma is an acquired neoplasm, it is extremely rare in newborns and children, as a rule – they appear in people older than 25-30 years. The multiplicity of the lesion is not characteristic (with the exception of some systemic diseases, hereditary syndromes, and HIV infection). By gender: dermatofibromas are more common in women.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of dermatofibromas. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_1_2: Damage to the skin, microtrauma, insect bites
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_1_3: Genetic factor: heredity can play a role in the appearance of dermatofibromas
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_2_1: The diagnosis of dermatofibroma is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_1: A visual examination of the dermatofibroma determines a slightly sunken (below the surface of the skin) or hemispherical formation, most often symmetrical (oval or round). The surface of the dermatofibroma is usually smoothed, the skin pattern is most often absent (especially in the center), less often small tuberosity, peeling.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_2: The boundaries of the dermatofibroma can be clear and even (in protruding hemispherical forms) or blurry (if the neoplasm is flat or sunken). Color varies from flesh, gray to shades of brown and crimson. The distribution of pigment throughout the formation is uneven: a gradual increase in color intensity is observed in the direction from the center to the periphery (the center of formation is lighter, even pale, the periphery of the formation is more intensely colored).
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_3: Hair in the central part of dermatofibroma is absent, but can occur on the periphery.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_4: The diameter of the dermatofibroma usually does not exceed 10 mm (larger formations are rarely found). The height above the skin for hemispherical forms is usually 5-7 mm.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_5: On palpation, the dermatofibroma is dense, firm. A distinctive feature is a symptom of the fossa: when the surrounding tissues are compressed, a depression is formed in the tumor area. There is no subjective sensation or mild itching (rarely).
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_3_6: They are located mainly on the lower extremities and in the shoulder girdle, other localizations are rarely observed.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the following dermatofibroma features are visualized:
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_2: Incorrect contour of the hypopigmented central zone
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_3: A light brown peripheral zone that surrounds the central zone
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_4: The peripheral zone is represented by a delicate pigment network with small cells
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_5: The boundaries of the peripheral zone smoothly pass into healthy skin
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_6: Fine-meshed uniform structure at the border of transition to healthy skin
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_4_7: Point vessels may rarely be detected.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_6_1: Dermatofibroma is safe and does not carry an increased risk of a malignant tumor. In the absence of external influences (trauma and other damaging factors) – the risk of malignant degeneration is comparable to the same risk on unchanged skin.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_6_2: Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the dermatofibroma, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, removal is not necessary, self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is sufficient at least once a year. If there was a mechanical damage to the dermatofibroma, changes in appearance were noticed, or previously absent sensations appeared, a dermatologist or oncologist should be consulted.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications for removal are set. It is necessary to remove those dermatofibromas that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_7_4: Patients, in the presence of other skin neoplasms (nevi) in combination with dermatofibroma, are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_8_2: Dermatofibroma treatment using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended, since in this case there is a pronounced tendency to local relapses.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of dermatofibromas and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_9_2: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_li_9_3: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
dermatofibroma.dermatofibroma_desc_9_2: Also, a regular examination of dermatofibromas, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms are necessary.

halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_1: Halo Nevus (Sutton’s Nevus) is a benign neoplasm towering above the skin, surrounded by a rim of hypopigmented skin. Most often, halo nevi are noted in persons 15–25 years of age: first a pigmented, central part appears, around which a colorless ring gradually expands. With age, the reverse involution of the central pigmented part of the nevus can occur (with the preservation of only the focus of hypopigmentation) or with its complete disappearance after 3-4 years.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of halo nevus. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor: the appearance of halo nevus may be due to the human genome
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_1_3: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet is capable of provoking the appearance of halo nevus
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_1_4: Autoimmune diseases: it is submitted that a depigmented ring is due to a secondary localized immune response to regional melanocytes, followed by their destruction
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of halo nevus is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_1: A visual examination of the halo nevus reveals a hemispherical, usually symmetrical (oval or round) formation rising above the skin, around which a rim of depigmented skin is noted. The focus of depigmentation is also regular oval or round in shape, symmetrical.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_2: The surface of the central (pigmented) part of the nevus is slightly different from the texture of the skin or finely tuberous. The surface of the focus of depigmentation is not changed (normal skin pattern).
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_3: The borders of the halo nevus are clear and even. The color of the central part varies from flesh, tan to dark brown, while the distribution of pigment throughout the formation is uniform. Sometimes there is a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery, or various shades of the same color within the formation. The color of the surrounding rim is uniform, often completely absent, less often light brown or pale pink or with slight hyperemia, however, the shade is unstable and can change over time. The colorless halo becomes more noticeable and contrast after tanning.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_4: The presence of halo nevus does not affect hair growth. Sometimes in the central part, there is a growth of single coarse bristly or fluffy hair.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_5: The diameter of the central pigmented part of the nevus usually does not exceed 10 mm. The total diameter of the halo nevus, taking into account the depigmented rim, can reach 3-4 cm. Over time, the diameter of the depigmentation focus can vary both in the direction of increase and decrease. The height of the protruding part of the nevus above the skin level usually does not exceed 3-4 mm.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_6: On palpation of the halo nevus, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin or slightly softer (central part). Subjective sensations are also absent.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_3_7: Neoplasms are located mainly on the body, less often – on any part of the body.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of the central part of the halo nevus, the following features can be visualized:
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_1: Cobblestone street – a network of oval pigment elements
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_2: Papillary structures – uneven tuberous structures, flattened due to pressure during dermatoscopy
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_4: Globules – large hyperpigmented ring structures that are evenly distributed throughout the nevus or in the center, are rarely found on the periphery (including gray-brown globules characteristic of hyperkeratosis)
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_5: Spots – hyperpigmented structureless areas located in the center
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_6: The pigment network is a pattern of hypopigmented holes and homogeneous lines from light brown to dark brown. The lines are evenly thinning to the periphery of the formation
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_7: Dots – are small hyperpigmented round structures that are located in the center or are found on the pigmented lines of the network
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_8: Vascular network – represented by slightly curved diffuse monomorphic vessels (regular vasculature)
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_4_9: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_5_2: With dermatoscopy of the depigmented area – the appearance of ordinary skin with the presence of barely noticeable or no pigment structures at all, perhaps a more marked regular vascular network.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_6_1: Halo nevus is safe and does not carry an increased risk of melanoma. If there is no external effect on such a nevus (trauma, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation), the risk of malignancy is comparable to the risk of a malignant tumor on unchanged skin. Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the halo nevus, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, self-control (or inspection with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is sufficient at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the nevus has occurred, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications are made for removal of the damaged nevus. It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_7_4: Patients with multiple moles are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are also recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of halo nevus using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
halo_nevus.halo_nevus_desc_9_2: Also, regular inspection of halo nevus, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms are necessary.

hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_1: Hemangioma – (angioma, vascular nevus) benign neoplasm formed by local accumulation and proliferation of small blood vessels (capillaries) on the skin. It is represented by a flat or slightly elevated formation of bright red color of various sizes and shapes. Hemangioma can be either congenital or acquired (appear throughout life). The multiplicity of the lesion is especially characteristic of small acquired hemangiomas, but there are also congenital multiple forms (hemangiomatosis). Equally common in males and females (congenital – more often in females).
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of hemangiomas. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms.
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_1_1_3: Maternal viral infections and various intoxications during pregnancy
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_2_1_5: Exposure to the skin of ultraviolet and ionizing radiation
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of hemangiomas is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_2_2: In the diagnosis of congenital hemangiomas, which can be deep, occupy a large area, located in the area of ​​vital organs and vascular structures, be part of congenital syndromes (for example: Sturge-Weber syndrome), an ultrasound diagnosis and a comprehensive examination by several related specialists are performed.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_1: A visual examination of hemangiomas can have significant differences.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_2: Congenital hemangiomas come in various shapes (oval, asymmetric, occupying a large area, and several anatomical areas). The surface is not changed (normal skin pattern), which is typical for flat, not protruding hemangiomas, smooth (smooth skin pattern), or slightly bumpy (typical for gross hemangiomas rising above the skin).
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_3: The boundaries of hemangiomas are clear, but often uneven (especially with large sizes, small with even contours). The color is represented by various shades of red (pink, bright red, raspberry, crimson, cyanotic), most often uniform throughout the area, but sometimes there are “spotting” or variegation. As a rule, it does not affect hair growth.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_4: The size of congenital hemangiomas can vary within wide limits: from point formations (2-3 mm) to large, occupying several anatomical areas (20-30 cm). On palpation, the hemangioma is soft, somewhat softer than the surrounding skin, the structure is more delicate. When pressed, it may fade. There are no subjective sensations. Hemangiomas are located mainly on the head (face, scalp), neck. Less commonly, other anatomical areas.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_5: Acquired hemangiomas usually have the appearance of a hemispherical (rarely on a wide stalk), symmetrical (oval or round) nodule that rises above the skin. The surface is slightly different from the texture of ordinary leather, but can be smoothed or even glossy.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_6: The boundaries are clear and even. The color is uniform, bright red, less often – other shades of red. It does not affect hair growth.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_3_7: Dimensions are usually small, up to 5-7 mm. Sometimes there are hemangional papillomas protruding above the skin, the height of which corresponds to the width. On palpation, the hemangioma is soft, from pressure, it turns pale. There are no subjective sensations. They are located mainly on the trunk and upper limbs, but can also be found on other parts of the body.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the following hemangioma features are visualized:
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_4_1: Symptoms of rigidity and filling – a sign of the elasticity of the tumor, which, when compressed, pales and decreases in size
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_4_2: After weakening the pressure, the formation acquires the former color and shape
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_4_3: A large number of small vascular (red) gaps, separated by thin blue jumpers
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_4_4: The presence of large blue-violet gaps is a sign of deep-lying venous hemangiomas
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_4_5: Blue-black and black-red lacunae with a yellow rim on the periphery are a sign of injured hemangioma with subsequent thrombosis of vascular lacunae.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_5_1: Various types of hemangiomas (congenital, acquired, as part of the syndromes, deep, superficial, etc.
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_5_6: Mushroom mycosis (T-cell lymphoma of the skin)
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_6_1: Hemangioma is safe and does not carry an increased risk of a malignant tumor. In the absence of external influences (trauma and other damaging factors) – the risk of malignant degeneration is comparable to the same risk on unchanged skin.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_6_2: Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_6_3: In addition to oncological risk, hemangioma (especially large sizes) can lead to rather massive bleeding if it is damaged. Also, large hemangiomas can ulcerate with the addition of an infection (with chronic injury, damage).
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_1: The tactics of managing hemangiomas depends on various factors.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_2: The decision on large congenital hemangiomas, as a rule, is made with the participation of doctors from various specialties: pediatricians, dermatologists, oncologists, surgeons, and others, if necessary. Indications for treatment and the timing of interventions are set individually depending on the effect of hemangiomas on the vital functions of the body. The issue of treatment priority in identifying other concomitant pathologies and disorders in the body is also important. When choosing tactics for dynamic observation (possibly with small superficial hemangiomas located on the trunk, limbs, in the absence of complications and rapid tumor growth), individual recommendations are formed.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_3: In the case of acquired small hemangiomas, in the absence of any damaging effects or changes in appearance and subjective sensations, removal is not necessary, self-monitoring (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is sufficient at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the hemangioma has occurred, changes in appearance have been noticed, or previously absent sensations have appeared, consultation with a dermatologist or oncologist is necessary.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_4: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications for removal are set. It is necessary to remove those hemangiomas that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the nature of professional employment.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_5: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_7_6: Patients, in the presence of other skin neoplasms (nevi) in combination with hemangiomas, are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_8_1: Less traumatic methods can be used to treat hemangiomas:
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_8_1: Laser treatment: the safest and most effective method, used for hemangiomas of various shapes, sizes and localization
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_8_2: Cryodestruction with liquid nitrogen: applicable for small superficial hemangiomas, the method is associated with a high risk of scarring
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_8_3: Subclinical hardening: applicable for small, delimited hemangiomas
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_8_2: If it is impossible to conduct less traumatic treatment, as well as in the event of life-threatening conditions (for example, bleeding), surgical removal of hemangiomas is used.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_8_3: Due to the high risk of recurrence of hemangiomas (especially congenital), repeated courses of treatment or operations are often required.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_8_4: For the treatment of congenital hemangiomas, in combination with the methods listed above, drug therapy is also used: beta-blockers (propranolol, atenolol, timolol (externally)), steroid hormones (prednisolone), antitumor drugs (vincristine).
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_9_1: Prevention of congenital hemangiomas is reduced to the proper management of pregnancy, minimizing stress and eliminating the use of drugs not recommended during pregnancy, to avoiding and timely treating infectious diseases, and eliminating smoking and alcohol consumption.
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_9_2: Prevention of the appearance of hemangiomas and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_9_2: Observance of safety measures during the work with the skin-damaging factors
hemangioma.hemangioma_li_9_4: Personal hygiene and basic awareness regarding skin neoplasms
hemangioma.hemangioma_desc_9_3: It also requires regular examination of all hemangiomas on the skin, timely consultation with a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_1: Papillomatous nevus (benign nevus, pigmented nevus, mole) is a benign neoplasm towering above the skin. As a rule, papillomatous nevus is acquired. With age, the number of formations increases, the peak of occurrence is noted at 15-30 years. This type of nevus is characterized by multiplicity, the proportion of which increases with age. By gender, nevi are somewhat more common in women compared with men, in a ratio of 3: 2, respectively.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of papillomatous nevi. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor: the appearance of papillomatous nevus may be due to the human genome
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_1_2: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet leads to faster reproduction of nevoid cells (nevus cells) and excessive production of melanin (pigment, the accumulation of which is noted in nevus)
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_1_3: Ionizing radiation, viral diseases, and injuries can also provoke the appearance or growth of papillomatous nevi.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of papillomatous nevi is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_1: A visual examination of the papillomatous nevus reveals a hemispherical formation rising above the skin or with a short wide leg, most often symmetrical (oval or round). Large nevi can be irregular in shape. The surface of the nevus is slightly different from the texture of ordinary skin or finely tuberous. Sometimes the papillomatous nevus looks like a coarse warty formation (the surface in the form of large, uneven papillae is the verrucous nevus), which is more typical for nevi from 8 mm or more.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_2: The borders of the papillomatous nevus are clear and even. Large nevi can be with uneven edges. The color of a simple nevus varies from flesh, tan to dark brown (almost black) in color, while the distribution of pigment throughout the formation is uniform. Sometimes there is a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery or different shades of the same color within the same formation (typical for verrucous nevus).
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_3: The presence of benign nevus does not affect hair growth. Less often in the area of ​​congenital nevus, there is a more intensive growth of coarse bristly hair, which is usually combined with pronounced brown pigmentation, or vice versa, downy hair (combined with hypopigmented papillomatous nevi).
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_4: The size of the nevi can vary within wide limits, however, the most common formations are up to 15 mm. Papillomatous nevi over 15 mm are rare. The height of such a nevus above the skin level usually does not exceed 10 mm. Papillomatous nevi in ​​the form of cauliflower and much larger sizes are rare.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_5: On palpation of a simple nevus, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin (larger formations) or slightly softer (formations up to 5 mm). Subjective sensations are also absent.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_3_6: Neoplasms are located mainly on the face, scalp, neck, trunk, and less commonly on the limbs.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of a papillomatous nevus, the following features are visualized:
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_1: Cobblestone street – a network of oval pigment elements;
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_2: Papillary structures – uneven tuberous structures, flattened due to pressure during dermatoscopy
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_3: Elasticity and deformation under pressure (as well as the first two points) are characteristic dermatoscopic signs of papillomatous nevi
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_4: Globules – large hyperpigmented ring structures that are evenly distributed throughout the nevus or in the center, are rarely found on the periphery (including gray-brown globules characteristic of hyperkeratosis)
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_5: Spots – hyperpigmented structureless areas located in the center
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_6: Vascular network – represented by slightly curved diffuse monomorphic vessels (regular vasculature)
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_4_7: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with pigmented neoplasms such as:
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_6_1: Papillomatous nevus is safe and does not carry an increased risk of melanoma. In the absence of external effects on such a nevus (trauma, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation), the risk of malignant degeneration is comparable to the risk of melanoma on unchanged skin. Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_6_2: A slightly increased risk of melanoma is observed in congenital nevus, but this is more typical for large pigmented lesions (more than 20 cm in diameter). The risk of melanoma on the background of congenital nevus up to 20 cm is less than 1%.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the papillomatous nevus, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the nevus has occurred, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications are made for removal of the damaged nevus. It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_7_4: Patients with multiple moles require an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are also recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of pigmented papillomatous nevus using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
papillomatous_nevus.papillomatous_nevus_desc_9_2: Also, regular inspection of pigmented papillomatous nevi, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms are necessary.

pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_1: Pyogenic granuloma (telangiectatic granuloma, botriomycoma, granulation Tissue-type Hemangioma, lobular capillary hemangioma, eruptive angioma, inflammatory hemangioma) is a benign neoplasm, which is a local reaction of blood capillaries in response to an external effect (most often an injury). Pyogenic granulomas appear in various parts of the body, including the mucous membranes, conjunctiva, and cornea. It is more common among young people as well as pregnant women.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of pyogenic granulomas. Among etiological factors, there are many versions. Previously, injuries (point injuries, cuts, foreign bodies, burns) were considered the main cause. However, today it is established that only 25% of all pyogenic granulomas appear against the background of injuries. Other possible causes include:
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_1_3: The presence of large burn surfaces
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_1_7: Pregnancy (Increased blood concentration of growth factors).
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of pyogenic granulomas is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_1: A visual examination of the pyogenic granuloma reveals a hemispherical formation rising above the skin or with a short wide leg, most often symmetrical (oval or round). The surface of the granuloma differs from the texture of ordinary skin: smooth or lobed (such as raspberries), shiny (“wet effect”), with erosion or crusts, with minor injury – it bleeds easily. Large granulomas after infection have become covered with purulent plaque with foci of necrosis.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_2: The boundaries of pyogenic granulomas are clear and even. The edge is represented by the epithelial corolla (the “collar” of the exfoliated epithelium). The color is bright red, cyanotic, cyanotic, in the presence of purulent plaque and foci of necrosis – dirty yellow, gray spots. When pressed, red shades fade.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_3: Hair in the area of ​​pyogenic granuloma usually does not grow.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_4: Dimensions are usually 3-15 mm. Formations over 15 mm are rare (with systemic diseases, immunodeficiency states, large burns, pressure sores). Granuloma growth within 1-1.5 cm is usually fast. The height of this above the skin level usually does not exceed 5 mm mm. Spontaneous (spontaneous) regression is rare, more characteristic of pregnant women after delivery.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_5: On palpation of pyogenic granuloma, a soft, elastic, painless nodule is determined. Subjective sensations are also absent. After infection, soreness may appear.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_3_6: Neoplasms are located mainly of the skin of the hands and feet, especially the palmar and plantar surfaces of the fingers (in the places of the most likely injury and contact with foreign bodies), in the area of ​​the nail ridges (against the background of an ingrown nail), on the face. Other areas, including mucous membranes, are rare (depending on predisposing factors: places of pressure sores, burns, injuries).
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of papillomatous nevus, the following features are visualized:
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_4_1: Symptoms of rigidity and filling – a sign of the elasticity of the tumor, which, when compressed, pales and decreases in size
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_4_2: After weakening the pressure, the formation acquires the former color and shape
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_4_3: A large number of small bright red vascular gaps
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such formations as:
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_6_1: With regard to cancer risks, pyogenic granuloma is safe. This formation does not carry an increased likelihood of malignant tumors. In the absence of external influences (injuries, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation) – the risk of malignancy is comparable to the risk of cancer on unchanged skin.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_6_2: In the absence of adequate care and treatment, pyogenic granuloma, especially of large sizes, is more dangerous for its complications in the form of infection and suppuration. In these situations, there is a risk of generalization of the infection with corresponding consequences. Also, from large granulomas, if they are damaged, bleeding may develop, which is difficult to cope on their own.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_6_3: Due to the fact that some malignant neoplasms may be similar in appearance to pyogenic granuloma or appear next to it, there is a certain degree of difficulty in timely differential diagnosis.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_7_1: If pyogenic granuloma is detected, a consultation with a dermatologist or oncologist is recommended. After differential diagnosis and elimination of cancer risks, the possibility of conservative management or the need for treatment is determined. Observation is possible only with small granulomas (a few millimeters), in pregnant women (there is a likelihood of spontaneous involution of education) or in the presence of another, more priority pathology that requires attention. In all other cases, the treatment of pyogenic granuloma is indicated.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_7_2: In case of refusal of the patient from treatment, active dynamic observation is necessary. At the same time, photo fixation of skin formation is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_7_3: Due to the fact that the presence of pyogenic granuloma can make it difficult to timely detect nearby or other tumors that are similar in appearance, but are more dangerous from the oncological point of view, such patients are shown to see a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before the beach season and after him). Of great importance is the mapping of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or changes to existing ones.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_8_1: The treatment of pyogenic granuloma is most often surgical: classical excision to the entire thickness of the skin or excision along the plane with the help of an electric or radio scalpel. After removal, a histological examination is mandatory.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_8_2: When the nature of the formation is not in doubt or a preliminary biopsy is performed with confirmation of the pyogenic granuloma, removal can be performed by laser coagulation, cryo destruction (removal by liquid nitrogen), or electrocoagulation (destruction of the granuloma by an electrocoagulator).
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_8_3: Since pyogenic granuloma is a vascular tumor, active bleeding may occur during removal. In this regard, after removal of the formation, it is necessary to achieve thorough hemostasis.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of pyogenic granuloma is a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_9_1: Exclusion of chronic trauma to the skin and burns
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_9_2: Limitation or exclusion of occupational hazards
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_9_3: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_9_4: Personal hygiene and basic awareness regarding skin neoplasms
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_li_9_5: Timely treatment of infectious diseases, including skin.
pyogenic_granuloma.pyogenic_granuloma_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of the skin, timely consultation with a specialist in the event of external changes in skin tumors, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_1: Spitz Nevus (Epithelioid and Spindle-Cell Nevus) – a benign neoplasm towering above the skin. As a rule, Spitz nevus is acquired (in 10% – congenital). About 70% of all cases are observed in people under the age of 20 years. Multiple lesions are noted sometimes. By gender, nevi are equally common among male and female patients.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of Spitz nevi. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor: the appearance of Spitz nevus may be due to the human genome
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_1_2: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet can provoke the appearance of new nevi
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_1_3: Hormonal changes: especially during puberty or during pregnancy
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of Spitz nevus is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_1: A visual examination of the Spitz nevus determines a hemispherical or flattened (rarely flat) formation rising above the skin, most often symmetrical (oval or round). The surface of the nevus is slightly different from the texture of ordinary skin or finely tuberous.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_2: The borders of the Spitz Nevus are clear and even. The color of a simple nevus varies from intense-bodily (light red) to brown or dark brown, while the distribution of pigment throughout the formation is uniform. Sometimes there is a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery, or various shades of the same color within the nevus.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_3: In the area of ​​Spitz nevus, hair never grows, which is a distinguishing feature of this formation and plays a significant role in differential diagnosis.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_4: The diameter of the Spitz nevus is usually 3-8 mm. The height above the skin usually does not exceed 5-7 mm.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_5: On palpation, the nevus is slightly denser than normal skin. There are no subjective sensations.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_3_6: They are located mainly on the face, neck, and limbs, less often – on the body.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the following Spitz nevus features are visualized:
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_4_1: Star pattern: the presence of pigment strips, dots and / or globules radially diverging from the center to the periphery – the main dermatoscopic symptom
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_4_2: Symmetric blue-white structure against the background of pigmented elements (often spots) in the center of the nevus
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_4_4: Vascular network – represented by slightly curved diffuse monomorphic vessels (regular vasculature)
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_4_5: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such pigmented neoplasms, as:
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_6_1: Spitz Nevus is safe and does not carry an increased risk of melanoma. In the absence of external effects on such a nevus (trauma, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation), the risk of malignant degeneration is comparable to the risk of melanoma on unchanged skin.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_6_2: Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations. The risk of melanoma on the background of congenital nevus is less than 1%.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the Spitz nevus, changes in appearance and subjective sensations – self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the nevus has occurred, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications are made for removal of the damaged nevus. It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_7_4: Patients with multiple moles require an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are also recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of Spitz nevus using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended.
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
spitz_nevus.spitz_nevus_desc_9_2: Also, a regular examination of Spitz nevi is necessary, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes and removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_1: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC, basal cell skin cancer) is a malignant tumor of the skin, a distinctive feature of which is a pronounced local destruction with almost no risk of metastasis. The low likelihood of metastases causes a relatively favorable prognosis of the disease, provided timely treatment. BCC is usually found at the age of over 35-40 years, equally often in men and women.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the occurrence of basal cell carcinoma. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of these neoplasms:
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_1_1: Excessive insolation: excessive exposure to solar ultraviolet
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_1_3: The influence of chemical compounds that damage the skin
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of basal cell cancer is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. After examination, a biopsy is performed.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_1: A visual examination of basal cell carcinoma determines a plaque or flattened protrusion protruding above the skin. On the surface, there are tuberosity, wartiness, ulceration, crusts. Upon contact, or even with a minor injury, bleeds easily.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_2: Borders are usually fuzzy (infiltrative growth) and uneven. The shape is often irregular, asymmetric, but sometimes the focus of the BCC is represented by a regular round or oval formation. It may look like a crater-like ulcer with a depression in the center (possibly even below the skin level) or vice versa, protruding above the skin and fixed to it by a wide pedicle formation.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_3: The color is pink, pink-red, with the application of horny masses – gray shades are added. In long-existing forms, foci of tissue necrosis with white-yellow, dirty-gray color may appear on the surface.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_5: Sizes range from 4 mm to 40 mm. Tumor enlargement is usually slow. In the absence of timely treatment, individual foci can reach large sizes, occupying entire anatomical areas.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_6: On palpation, a more dense formation is defined in comparison with the surrounding skin.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_7: Subjective sensations are usually absent. There is no morbidity with mechanical action on the tumor itself. When subcutaneous structures are involved in the tumor process, pain may appear.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_3_8: Foci of basal cell carcinoma are located mainly in open areas of the body and areas most often exposed to insolation: head (especially the face), neck, upper limbs, back, lower legs. Slightly less often the area of ​​the chest, abdomen, and thighs.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the most reliable symptoms and signs of basal cell carcinoma include:
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_4_1: Pathological vessels in the form of tree branching
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_4_3: Spherical inclusions of a pigment of a blue-gray color and a point
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_4_4: Unstructured zones of red, pink or white pigmentation
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_6_1: Despite the fact that basal cell skin cancer is a malignant tumor, the prognosis after timely and correct treatment is relatively favorable. This is due to the almost complete absence of the possibility of tumor metastasis. Only the likelihood of local recurrence remains or the risk of new cases of BCC in a different location increases slightly. Local relapses or multiple tumors, with proper treatment, do not worsen the prognosis.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_6_2: The risk of relapse in the same place depends on the size of basal cell carcinoma and the depth of its invasion of the skin. As well as the volume and adequacy of surgical treatment.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_6_3: BCC can appear both on healthy skin and on the background of existing benign or precancerous neoplasms. In the latter case, there is a certain degree of difficulty in timely differential diagnosis and detection of malignant transformation.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_6_4: In recent years, the incidence of BCC has been increasing: by about 10% in 5 years.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_7_1: If a suspicion is detected or if the first signs of basal cell skin cancer are detected, an oncologist should be consulted. The oncologist conducts additional specifying tests. In the absence of sufficient clinical data for an unambiguous diagnosis, sometimes the tactics of active dynamic observation is chosen. More often, a suspicious lesion or biopsy is performed, followed by histological examination.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_7_2: With histological confirmation of BCC, a standard list of examinations is assigned to search or exclude the presence of metastases, after which a special treatment plan is formed.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_7_3: In this regard, in patients with the presence of CCB, the risk of other malignant tumors increases – a regular thorough examination of the skin is recommended. When suspicious neoplasms are detected, a positive role is played by their photo fixation, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance. In the same situations, an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before the beach season and after it) is indicated. Of great importance is the mapping of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or changes to existing ones.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_8_1: The main treatment method is surgical: wide excision of the tumor focus. This is the most effective method with a low risk of local recurrence.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_8_2: Another effective and universally recognized method is short-focus x-ray therapy (radiation therapy). It is usually used to treat foci up to 20 mm.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_8_3: The use of other methods of local exposure (laser removal or cryodestruction) even of the earliest forms is unacceptable. The tumor should be removed radically, within healthy skin, without damaging the tumor focus itself. Otherwise, the risk of local relapse increases.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_8_4: Today, methods are being developed for the local use of cytostatics (chemotherapy). However, there is no unequivocal opinion regarding such treatment due to the fact that these methods increase the duration of treatment of skin cancer, the cost, the damaging effect on the healthy surrounding skin and have dubious radicalism when used improperly. Such treatment should be carried out under the strict supervision of a specialist. On the other hand, local treatment with the help of certified and approved by oncologists means has a good cosmetic result.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of basal cell skin cancer and its progression is gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
basal_cell_carcinoma.basal_cell_carcinoma_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of the skin, timely consultation with a specialist in the event of external changes in skin tumors, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_1: Lentigo melanoma is an aggressive malignant tumor. It develops from melanocytes (cells containing the pigment melanin) on the background of Dubreus melanosis. Lentigo melanoma is typical for the elderly age and often appears in open areas of the body (face). There is a long course and a relatively favorable prognosis (when compared with other forms of melanoma) with timely treatment. In the structure of all melanomas, the incidence of lentigo-melanoma is about 5%.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_2: The aggressiveness of lentigo-melanoma is due to the ability of this tumor to frequent relapses and metastasis in almost all organs. The metastasis pathway can be either lymphogenous or hematogenous. The rapid progression of melanoma also depends on the state of the body’s natural antitumor immunity.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3: Most often, lentigo melanoma appears over the age of 50 years. At an earlier age is rare.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_4: Various factors lead to the transformation of normal melanocytic cells into malignant melanoma cells.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_5: Factors that increase the risk of lentigo melanoma
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_6: Lentigo melanoma usually appears against the background of Dubreus melanosis, a precancerous skin disease that is a pigmented, light brown, multiform spot. Dubreus melanosis develops under the influence of active exposure to solar ultraviolet, adverse weather conditions for the skin, and chronic injury.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_7: There are a number of other factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of lentigo-melanoma (malignancy of Dubreus melanosis):
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_1_2: White/fair skin (I-II phototypes of the skin), the presence of pink freckles
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_1_5: Frequent sunburn, including a medical history (especially dangerous sunburn up to 14 years old)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_1_6: A burdened hereditary history of melanoma (genetic factor)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_1_9: Sporadic or chronic injury to foci of melanosis.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_2_1: Sporadic or chronic injury to foci of melanosis.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_1: On visual inspection of lentigo-melanoma, a multiform formation in the form of a spot is determined. The surface of melanoma is usually different from the texture of ordinary skin. Only in the very early stages (zero or first) the skin pattern can not be disturbed. In other cases, a rougher surface, peeling, small tuberosity is noted. In advanced cases, an exophytic component appears, weeping, ulceration, bleeding.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_2: Visual assessment of pigmented lesions suspicious of lentigo melanoma is primarily carried out using the ABCDE system (Friedman, 1985):
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_3: A – asymmetry, asymmetry of the tumor
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_4: B – border, the state of the edge of the tumor
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_7: E – evolving, the evolution (change) of a tumor over time.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_8: Asymmetry is an irregular form of a pigmented neoplasm. It is determined by drawing a conditional line through the center of the tumor, while one half will not be a mirror image of the other half.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_9: The edges of lentigo-melanoma (border with healthy skin) are uneven. In surface forms, the edge is usually clear (favorable factor), when an invasion appears (vertical growth, “immersion” in the skin), the edge becomes less clear, blurred (unfavorable factor).
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_10: The color of lentigo melanoma is quite variable within the formation. The simultaneous presence of various shades of brown is possible: from light brown to dark, up to black. Usually, especially in early forms, shades of brown (coffee) color prevail. Over time, the proportion of dark areas increases. The distribution of the pigment is heterogeneous (color heterogeneity over the entire area), asymmetric, with areas up to the complete absence of pigment (areas of regression, unfavorable factor). In addition to brown, other colors or their shades (polychrome) may be present: blue, blue, pink-red, white.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_11: The sizes of detected foci of lentigo-melanoma are usually more than 10 mm due to the fact that this type of malignant tumor appears against the background of an existing pigment formation. Smaller foci, due to long horizontal growth and small thickness of the tumor, are clinically difficult to determine.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_12: The behavior of lentigo melanoma over time is rather mixed. Most often, this is a slow increase in the area of ​​the tumor due to the long, stretching for years, phase of horizontal growth. Acceleration is observed during the transition to the phase of vertical growth (deep into the skin). The evolution (change) of pigment formation also includes:
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_1_1: The loss of previously present hair in the area of ​​the age spots
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_1_2: The appearance of subjective sensations (itching, burning, tingling)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_1_4: Surface changes (smoothing of the skin pattern, the appearance of tuberosity, roughness, ulceration, cracks or exophytic component)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_1_6: The rapid disappearance of part or all of the pigmentation, especially after ultraviolet radiation
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_13: For later and neglected lentigo melanomas, it is typical:
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_2_1: The appearance of nearby similar, but smaller foci (intradermal metastases)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_3_2_2: The presence of enlarged and dense lymph nodes along the lymphatic vessels (regional metastasis zone)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_14: The presence of at least one of the above symptoms is already an indication for consultation with a dermatologist or oncologist. The presence of three signs at the same time – the probability of lentigo-melanoma reaches 80% or more.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_3_15: The main localization of lentigo-melanoma is the face or other exposed areas of the body. The appearance of lentigo-melanoma in other anatomical areas is very rare.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of lentigo-melanoma, multicomponentity is visualized (the simultaneous presence of a large number of different pathological patterns):
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_4_1: Pigment network heterogeneity (atypical pigment network) – different intensity and eccentricity
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_4_3: The presence of irregular inclusions of points and globules against the background of the pigment network (eccentric clusters)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_4_4: Globules of various shapes, sizes and colors
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_4_5: Asymmetry in color, structure and shape
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_4_9: The presence of hypopigmentation zones and structureless zones, regression structures (unfavorable factor)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_6_1: Lentigo melanoma is one of the most dangerous malignant tumors. In the world, approximately every 7 years, there is a double increase in the number of primary cases of melanoma. This is due, first of all, to an increase in the intensity of insolation and to a more frequent appearance of people in climatic zones unusual for their skin.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_6_2: The appearance of lentigo-melanoma against the background of an already existing pigment neoplasm (Dubreus melanosis) to some extent complicates the timely differential diagnosis and detection of malignant transformation.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_6_3: Despite the fact that melanoma is approximately 10 times less common than other malignant skin tumors, mortality in the first case is 3.5 times higher.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_7_1: If a suspicion is detected or the first signs of lentigo-melanoma are detected, an oncologist should be consulted. The oncologist conducts additional specifying tests. In the absence of sufficient clinical data for an unambiguous diagnosis, sometimes the tactics of active dynamic observation is chosen. Most often, excision of a suspicious lesion is performed, followed by histological examination.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_7_2: When confirming lentigo-melanoma (clinically or histologically), a standard list of examinations is assigned to search for or exclude the presence of metastases, after which a special treatment plan is formed.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_8_1: In most cases, the treatment is surgical. Standard practice is a wide excision of melanoma under anesthesia or conduction anesthesia (if tumor localization allows this). If metastases are detected in regional lymph nodes, lymph dissection is performed (removal of the entire block of regional lymph nodes). If distant metastases are detected, the treatment regimen is selected individually. For this, the oncologists’ arsenal has quite effective chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation therapy regimens, as well as the possibility of surgical removal or minimally invasive therapy of metastases.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_8_2: Treatment of lentigo-melanoma (even the earliest forms) with local destruction methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) or removal under local anesthesia is unacceptable.
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of lentigo-melanoma is a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (natural (sun) and artificial)
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
lentigo_melanoma.lentigo_melanoma_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of all pigmented neoplasms, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous tumors.

melanoma.melanoma_li_2: Nodular: more typical for men, the prognosis is often unfavorable due to the large depth of invasion of the skin (15%)
melanoma.melanoma_li_3: Acrolentiginous or subungual melanoma: more typical for dark-skinned individuals. In addition to the nail bed, it is located at the fingertips and palms (10%)
melanoma.melanoma_li_4: Lentiginous melanoma: more characteristic of women, appears against the background of age spots of lentigo, melanosis. The prognosis is often favorable due to the small depth of invasion of the skin (5%)
melanoma.melanoma_desc_4: Most often, melanoma appears in middle age (30-50 years). At an earlier age is extremely rare. For the older age group, lentiological forms of melanoma are especially characteristic.
melanoma.melanoma_desc_5: Various factors lead to the transformation of normal melanocytic cells into malignant melanoma cells.

Most often, patients seek medical help with 8-15 mm melanomas, although there are tumors up to 10 cm.
melanoma.melanoma_desc_3_7: The behavior of melanoma over time is rather mixed. Most often, this is a rapid growth in a few months. However, the horizontal growth phase (surface-spreading form) can last several years. Acceleration is observed during the transition to the phase of vertical growth. An assessment of the growth rate is quite informative when compared with the growth of other pigmented lesions (nevi) on the body. The evolution (change) of pigment formation also includes:

squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_1: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin (SCC) is a malignant tumor of the skin with germination in the dermis and the development of severe local destruction. It has a dubious prognosis due to the fact that there is a likelihood of metastasis. Pathology usually occurs at the age of over 35-40 years, equally often in men and women.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_1_1: There is no clear cause for squamous cell carcinoma. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of these neoplasms:
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_li_1_1: Excessive insolation: excessive exposure to solar ultraviolet
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_li_1_3: The influence of chemical compounds that damage the skin
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_li_1_5: Some dermatological diseases: Mibelli’s porokeratosis, dystrophic bullous epidermolysis, lichen planus, lupus erythematosus, Lewandowski-Lutz epidermodysplasia
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_li_1_6: The role of human papillomavirus in increasing the risk of Bowen’s disease is not ruled out
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_2_1: The diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. After examination, a biopsy is performed.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_1: A visual examination of squamous cell carcinoma determines a plaque or flattened protrusion protruding above the skin. On the surface, there are tuberosity, wartiness, ulcerations, crusts, hyperkeratosis. Upon contact, or even with a minor injury, bleeds easily.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_2: Borders are usually fuzzy (infiltrative growth) and uneven. The shape is often irregular, asymmetric, but sometimes the focus of squamous cell carcinoma is represented by a regular round or oval formation. It may look like a crater-like ulcer with a depression in the center (possibly even below the skin level) or vice versa, protruding above the skin and fixed to it by a wide pedicle formation.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_3: The color is pink, pink-red, with the appearance of horny masses – gray shades join, the intensity of which depends on the severity of keratosis in the tumor area. In long-existing forms, foci of tissue necrosis with white-yellow, dirty-gray color may appear on the surface.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_5: Sizes range from 4 mm to 40 mm with rapid tumor growth. In the absence of timely treatment, individual foci can reach large sizes, occupying entire anatomical areas.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_6: On palpation, a more dense formation is defined in comparison with the surrounding skin.
squamous_cell.squamous_cell_desc_3_7: Subjective sensations are usually absent. There is no morbidity with mechanical action on the tumor itself. When subcutaneous structures are involved in the tumor process, pain may appear.
