pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2: The key point in the diagnosis is the clinical picture and the patient’s complaints in conjunction with typical pathognomonic (specific for pustular psoriasis) signs.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_3: The main therapeutic principles include keratolysis (with the help of urea or salicylic acid preparations), as well as a decrease in the inflammatory response and hyperproliferation of keratinocytes (includes local and systemic treatment with various groups of drugs).
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_4: There are several types of pustular psoriasis:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_1: Generalized pustular psoriasis (von Zumbusch pustular psoriasis)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_2: Palmoplantar psoriasis (chronic persistent palmoplantar pustulosis, Barbera pustular psoriasis, limb pustular psoriasis)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_3: Annular pustular psoriasis, or annular pustulosis
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_4: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans (palmar and plantar psoriasis)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_1_1: Unlike psoriasis vulgaris, the cause of pustular psoriasis is unknown. The relationship with trigger factors has not been established or proven insufficient. Somewhat more often, this type of psoriasis occurs in people who smoke. Genetic causes are also rare.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_1_2: Sometimes pustular psoriasis forms against the background of common, vulgar psoriasis. Factors provoking the transformation of psoriasis vulgaris into pustular psoriasis include:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_1_1: Taking a number of drugs: systemic corticosteroids, cytotoxic drugs, salicylates, antidepressants, hydroxychloroquine, calcipotriol, chemotherapy drugs, anabolics, uncontrolled NSAIDs, penicillin antibiotics, progesterone, beta-blockers, oral contraceptives
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_1_2: Powerful skin irritants: chemical, biological, physical
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_1_4: Conditions leading to suppression of immunity (infectious and other severe concomitant diseases)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_1_5: Long-term exposure to sunlight, ultraviolet light.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2_1: Pustular psoriasis is manifested by the presence of raised vesicles or blisters (pustules) on the surface of the skin, which are filled with a clear liquid (exudate). The skin around is not changed, however, under and above the surface of the pustules and around them, the skin is red, of a higher temperature, swollen, inflamed and thickened, easily exfoliates.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2_2: In the case of the addition of a secondary infection (infection of the pustules), the contents become more turbid (up to the appearance of purulent discharge), the signs of inflammation are more pronounced.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2_3: Pustular psoriasis is located most often on the distal ends of the limbs (arms and legs), that is, on the legs and forearms. This form is called palmoplantar pustulosis (localized pustular psoriasis).
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2_4: In more severe cases, pustular psoriasis can be generalized, with widespread pustules over the entire surface of the body and a tendency to merge into larger pustules.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_2_5: Psoriasis is a chronic disease with a recurrent course: periods of exacerbation are replaced by asymptomatic intervals of varying duration.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_3_1: Typically, the diagnosis of pustular psoriasis is clinical. The physical examination is based on examination and identification of the characteristic psoriatic pustules.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_3_2: Characteristic psoriatic plaques can also be detected, and there is the psoriatic triad of Auspitz:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_3_1: The “stearin spot” phenomena (free discharge of scales from the surface of papules)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_3_2: The phenomenon of the “terminal film” (reddish shiny surface in the place of removed scales)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_3_3: The phenomenon of capillary bleeding (after scraping the red surface, pinpoint bleeding occurs)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_3_3: In doubtful cases, a biopsy of the affected skin area can be performed for histological confirmation of the diagnosis, as well as culturing of contents from vesicles or blisters.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_4_1: Pustular psoriasis must be differentiated from diseases such as dermatophytosis of the hands and feet, eczema of the hands and feet, dyshidrotic eczema, keratoderma, toxicoderma, squamous-hyperkeratotic forms of mycosis of the feet and palms.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_4_2: Generalized pustular psoriasis is differentiated from bacteremia and sepsis by blood.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_1: The main goal of treatment for pustular psoriasis is to reduce the severity of symptoms and improve the patient’s quality of life.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_2: The basic principles of therapy include:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_5_1: Primary keratolysis as a basic local therapy (preparations containing urea and salicylic acid, moisturizing creams)
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_5_3: Reducing the severity of the inflammatory process on the skin
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_3: As a local treatment, in addition to basic drugs (urea + salicylic acid), calcineurin inhibitors, topical glucocorticoids, calciferol, and retinoids are prescribed.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_4: The indications for the appointment of systemic therapy are:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_5_6: Inadequate response to topical treatment or phototherapy
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_5: In this case, retinoids, fumaric acid esters, immunosuppressants, biotherapy (adalimumab, secukinumab, apremilast, etc.) are prescribed. Also, detoxification therapy is prescribed, correction of vital blood parameters and the function of other organs.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_5_6: In physiotherapy, phototherapy seems to be the main focus.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_6_1: Complications are more pronounced and dangerous compared to psoriasis vulgaris. Against the background of pustular psoriasis, the following complications can develop:
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_6_3: Onycholysis – destruction of the nail plate
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_6_4: Decrease in the level of albumin and the level of calcium in the blood and their consequences depending on the severity of the deficiency
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_li_6_5: Kidney damage up to renal tubular necrosis with the development of renal failure
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_6_2: Severe complications of generalized pustular psoriasis can cause severe intoxication with subsequent multiple organ failure and death. Complications occur in 17%, deaths occur in 2% of cases.
pustular_psoriasis.pustular_psoriasis_desc_7_1: To reduce the risk of developing pustular psoriasis and, to a greater extent, to prevent exacerbations, it is recommended to avoid trigger factors, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, exclude mechanical skin irritants, monitor body weight, lead a healthy lifestyle (regular physical activity), timely treat concomitant diseases and exclude uncontrolled intake of medicines (without a doctor’s prescription).

psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_1: Psoriasis vulgaris, also known as chronic stationary psoriasis or plaque-like psoriasis, is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder that is scaling on sharply defined red plaques. Often, skin changes are accompanied by itching in combination with changes in the nail plate.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_2: The manifestation of the disease is based, on the one hand, on a polygenic predisposition, on the other, on exogenous and endogenous trigger factors (for example, infections, drugs, mechanical irritation).
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_3: The key point in the diagnosis is the clinical picture and the patient’s complaints in conjunction with typical pathognomonic (psoriasis-specific) signs.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_4: The main therapeutic principles include keratolysis (with the help of urea or salicylic acid preparations), as well as a decrease in the inflammatory response and hyperproliferation of keratinocytes (includes local and systemic treatment with various groups of drugs).
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_1_1: Psoriasis is equally common in both men and women. The approximate distribution is 1-2% of the population. Age does not affect the risk of psoriasis. However, depending on age, psoriasis of the first and second types is distinguished:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_1_1: Type I – the onset of morbidity at the age of 20-30 (associated with impaired immune processes that are inherited)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_1_2: Type II – onset of morbidity after 50 years (not associated with heredity)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_2_1: Psoriasis can have a genetic predisposition (hereditary factor), occur against a background of concomitant pathology (more often – autoimmune diseases, anxiety disorders), or be provoked by various triggers:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_2_2: Infectious diseases (not only of the skin, but also of internal organs, for example, the upper respiratory tract
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_2_3: Taking certain medications: beta-blockers, chloroquine, lithium preparations, interferon
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_3_1: Psoriasis is a chronic disease with a recurrent course: periods of exacerbation are replaced by asymptomatic intervals of varying duration.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_3_2: During the period of exacerbation, erythematosquamous plaques appear in the form of sharply outlined redness with underlying skin infiltration and tight-fitting large-lamellar scales of a silvery-white color.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_3_1: The extensor sides of the limbs, especially the elbows and knees
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_3_3: The trunk, especially the sacrum and umbilical region
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_3_4: The face, incl. external auditory canal
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_3_5: Palms and soles of the feet
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_3_7: Nails: There can be one single pit or many pits. A nail with multiple pits can look like the surface of a thimble, partial and predominantly distal detachment of the nail from the nail bed, the presence of subungual hemorrhages, nail dystrophy in the form of destruction of the nail plate, the appearance of roughness and turbidity
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_3_4: Itching occurs in about 60% of patients.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_4_1: As a rule, the diagnosis of psoriasis is made clinically (by examination).
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_4_2: Physical examination is based on examination and identification of characteristic psoriatic plaques, with the Auspitz psoriatic triad:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_4_1: The phenomenon of stearin spot (free discharge of scales from the surface of papules)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_4_2: Terminal film phenomenon (reddish shiny surface in the place of removed scales)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_4_3: The phenomenon of capillary bleeding (after scraping the red surface, pinpoint bleeding occurs)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_4_3: In doubtful cases, a biopsy of the affected skin area can be performed for histological confirmation of the diagnosis.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_4_4: To assess the severity of psoriatic skin lesions, the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) is used. This is a system for assessing the area of ​​skin lesions and the severity of the main symptoms. If PASI ≤10 – psoriasis of mild degree, in case of PASI> 10 – a diagnosis of moderate or severe psoriasis is made.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_5_1: As a rule, the clinical picture of classic (vulgar) psoriasis is quite clear and understandable. However, in certain forms of the disease, such as generalized pustular psoriasis or psoriatic erythroderma, it is necessary to carry out differential diagnosis with diseases such as:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_6_1: The main goal of treatment for psoriasis is to reduce the severity of symptoms and improve the patient’s quality of life. At PASI ≤10, topical preparations are usually sufficient. When PASI> 10, a combination of local, systemic therapy and physiotherapy is prescribed.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_6_2: The basic principles of psoriasis therapy include:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_6_1: Primary keratolysis as a basic local therapy (preparations containing urea and salicylic acid, moisturizing creams)
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_6_3: Reducing the severity of the inflammatory process on the skin
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_6_3: As a local treatment, in addition to basic drugs (urea + salicylic acid), calcineurin inhibitors, topical glucocorticoids, calciferol, and retinoids are prescribed.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_6_4: The indications for the appointment of systemic therapy are:
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_6_4: Severe psoriasis with a PASI index> 10
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_li_6_6: Inadequate response to topical or phototherapy
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_6_5: In this case, retinoids, fumaric acid esters, immunosuppressants, biotherapy (adalimumab, secukinumab, apremilast, etc.) are prescribed. In physiotherapy, phototherapy seems to be the main focus.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_7_1: The most frequent complications of psoriasis (usually after a severe and prolonged course) are cardiovascular diseases: hypertension, coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction, acute cerebrovascular accident.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_7_2: In addition to the effects on the cardiovascular system, metabolic syndrome, obesity and other metabolic problems can occur.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_7_3: Bacterial infection of psoriasis foci is not typical.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_7_4: The prognosis for life is favorable, but due to complaints and social stigmatization in patients with psoriasis, the quality of life is significantly reduced.
psoriasis_vulgaris.psoriasis_vulgaris_desc_8_1: To reduce the risk of developing psoriasis and, to a greater extent, to prevent exacerbations, it is recommended to avoid trigger factors, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, exclude mechanical skin irritants, monitor body weight, lead a healthy lifestyle (regular physical activity), timely treat concomitant diseases and exclude uncontrolled intake of medicines (without a doctor’s prescription).

seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1: Seborrheic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder that causes redness, dryness, and scaling. The disease usually affects those areas of the skin where the greatest number of sebaceous glands: scalp, face, ears. It can also lead to the formation of thick areas of dry skin. Symptoms range from mild to severe.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_2: Seborrheic dermatitis occurs in infants as well as in older children and adults. This skin disorder is not contagious, nor does it cause damage or hair loss, but it can be a serious cosmetic problem.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1_1: There is no definite reason for the development of seborrheic dermatitis.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1_2: In infants, seborrheic dermatitis may be caused by the gradual disappearance of hormones transmitted by the mother before delivery.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1_3: Yeast-like fungi, which occur on the surface of healthy skin with a frequency of up to 80%, may play a role in the onset of this disease.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1_4: Common triggers can also exacerbate or provoke the development of seborrheic dermatitis:
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_1_5: Harsh detergents, solvents, chemicals and soaps
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_1_5: Other factors that increase the risk of developing seborrheic dermatitis:
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_1_6: Age: children under 3 months and adults over 60 years old
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_1_7: Diseases: HIV, acne, rosacea or psoriasis, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_1_8: Suppression of the immune system: taking immunosuppressants after organ transplantation, chemotherapy
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_1_9: Other conditions: alcoholism, depression, eating disorders
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_3_1: Seborrheic dermatitis can appear on almost any part of the body, but most often it affects the scalp, eyelashes, eyebrows, and the area of ​​the nasolabial triangle. The upper chest, back, groin and axillary regions are also frequently affected.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_4_1: When the first signs of seborrheic dermatitis appear, you should consult a dermatologist. This is due to the fact that more serious diseases can begin with similar signs, such as:
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_4_6: Systemic lupus erythematosus (similarity to erythema of the “butterfly” type)
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_4_2: To differentiate these conditions, in addition to a medical history and examination, a dermatologist may perform skin scrapings or other tests.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_4_3: Also, consultation with a dermatologist is necessary in case of exacerbation of seborrheic dermatitis in order to prescribe timely treatment, to exclude the progression and development of complications.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_5_1: Mostly in adults (and usually in more severe cases), if left untreated, seborrheic dermatitis can develop a secondary bacterial infection. This is manifested by more pronounced hyperemia, soreness of the skin, the occurrence of wetness.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_5_2: Another possible complication of seborrheic dermatitis is associated with side effects of treatment (for example, from the prescribed topical corticosteroids: thinning of the skin and the appearance of telangiectasias – the expansion of blood vessels).
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_5_3: In adults, seborrheic dermatitis is often a chronic condition that requires periodic treatment to relieve symptoms and reduce the likelihood of recurrence of flare-ups.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_6_1: The doctor makes the diagnosis based on the medical history and examination, paying particular attention to the face and scalp. If the diagnosis is unclear or the patient does not respond to treatment, other clarifying manipulations are performed, up to biopsy and histological examination.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_7_1: Treatment depends on the location of the dermatitis and the severity of the symptoms. With seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp in both children and adults, special shampoos are prescribed. Before rinsing off the shampoo, the scales that are least fixed to the skin can be removed with a soft brush.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_7_2: If the scales are not easily removed, you can apply a few drops of mineral oil to the scalp before cleaning and shampooing. A medicated cream is sometimes used, especially for severe dermatitis. For mild symptoms, a non-drug cream is prescribed to keep the skin moist.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_desc_7_3: If the specific nature of dermatitis (for example, fungal) is identified, appropriate treatment is prescribed.
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_1: Cleanse your skin daily with mild soap or dandruff shampoo (baby shampoo)
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_2: Soften scaly skin with mineral oil or olive oil and leave the oil on the skin for about an hour, then gently brush off the scales and wash the skin
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_3: Avoid using hair styling products during treatment
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_4: Avoid foods containing alcohol, as this can exacerbate seborrheic dermatitis
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_5: To reduce irritation, wear cotton clothing
seborrheic_dermatitis.seborrheic_dermatitis_li_7_6: If you have symptoms of seborrheic dermatitis around your eyelids, rinse your eyelids every night with baby shampoo and wipe off flaky skin with a cotton swab

actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_1: Actinic keratosis (AK, solar keratosis) is a benign skin tumor in the form of a fuzzy hyperemic spot with keratinization. Actinic keratosis has a high risk of transformation into squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, therefore, refers to an optional precancerous condition. These formations appear, as a rule, over the age of 40 in open areas of the body that are exposed to frequent and prolonged exposure to solar ultraviolet light. Actinic keratosis is characterized by plurality, the area of ​​skin lesion increases with age. Equally common in both men and women.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of actinic keratosis. However, solar ultraviolet and increased susceptibility to its damaging effects on the skin of older people are considered the main provocative factor. Due to the fact that the damaging effects of solar ultraviolet radiation have a cumulative effect, AK can appear even many years after active insolation.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_1_2: Other factors that, to varying degrees, may increase the risk of actinic keratosis include:
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_1_5: The presence of immunodeficiency states: due to the use of immunosuppressants, chemotherapy for cancer, after severe infections
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_1_6: Genetic factor: the appearance of AK may be due to the human genome
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_1_7: Ionizing radiation, the influence of chemical compounds, chronic injuries can also provoke the appearance or growth of keratosis
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of actinic keratosis is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_1: A visual examination of actinic keratosis identifies single, multiple, or grouped spots or plaques. The surface of the plaque differs significantly from the texture of ordinary skin: rough, focal covered with crusts, sometimes with signs of erosion and bruising.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_2: The borders are fuzzy and uneven. The shape is irregular, asymmetric. The color is nude, gray, gray-brown with the presence of pink or pink-red shades.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_3: Actinic keratosis, as a rule, does not affect hair growth.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_4: Sizes range from 5 mm to 20 mm. Grouped structures of several plaques can reach 3-4 cm.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_5: On palpation, a hard, dry formation with peeling is determined. Subjective sensations are usually absent or mild itching.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_3_6: The preferred localization of actinic keratosis is facial skin (especially the protruding parts: the tip of the nose, auricles, frontal tubercles, zygomatic areas). Also, with great frequency, the scalp, neck, upper limbs (the area of ​​the shoulder girdle, and wrist) are affected – those places that are most exposed to insolation.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of actinic keratosis, the following features are visualized:
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_4_2: Red pseudo-network (reticular structure formed by vessels)
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_4_5: Yellowish keratotic plugs (horny masses) in the expanded hair follicles
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_4_6: Vascular structures: mainly convoluted and linear
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_4_7: Dark brown veins, dots and brown globules in pigmented forms of actinic keratosis
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such pigmented neoplasms, such as:
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_6_1: Actinic keratosis is an optional precancerous condition. The risk of malignant transformation reaches 20%. Malignancy can occur both independently and under the influence of additional external factors (chronic injury, thermal and chemical burns). In the case of malignancy, actinic keratosis is more often transformed into squamous cell (squamous) cancer. Sometimes this happens through a clinically determined phase of Bowen’s disease.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_6_2: Must be taken into account that patients with severe actinic keratosis have an increased risk of developing a malignant tumor on unchanged skin or near the focus of keratosis. This can complicate the timely detection and differential diagnosis of tumors.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the foci of actinic keratosis, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage has occurred, active exposure to ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the keratoma itself are noticed or previous sensations – consultation with a dermatologist or oncologist is needed.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic observation (terms are determined individually) or indications are set for the removal of damaged skin formation. It is necessary to remove those plaques that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_7_4: Patients with actinic keratosis require an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_1: Due to the fact that actinic keratosis has a rather high risk of transformation into squamous cell carcinoma, along with active dynamic observation, AK treatment is also indicated. Any effects on the foci of keratosis should be carried out only after the exclusion of the fact of malignancy (after examination by an oncologist, dermatoscopy, or biopsy).
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_2: First of all, it is necessary to protect the skin from UV radiation: clothing, hats, limiting insolation, sunscreens. These measures significantly reduce the progression of keratosis and its malignant degeneration.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_3: Possible local removal of plaques using local destruction methods (laser, cryodestruction, diathermocoagulation). The use of such methods is also not recommended if it is impossible to conduct a clear differential diagnosis with neoplasms of a pigmented nature (pigmented, dysplastic and other nevi).
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_4: Surgical treatment by excision is rarely used due to the frequent presence of a large number and large sizes of foci of keratosis, as well as cosmetic consequences in the form of scars. However, this method has an advantage in cases where it is difficult to exclude malignancy.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_5: There are a number of drugs and techniques that can also be used for topical use in the treatment of actinic keratosis:
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_8_6: Combined procedures in combination with cosmetic products
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_8_6: However, the application of these methods should be carried out only under the careful and long-term supervision of specialists, it does not always have unambiguously proven efficacy, side effects, high risks of relapse and low availability for a wide range of patients.
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of actinic keratosis and its malignancy is gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
actinic_keratosis.actinic_keratosis_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of keratosis foci, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_1: blue nevus (blue nevus of Jadassohn–Tièche, blue neuronevus, dermal melanocytoma) is a benign skin neoplasm with a characteristic color from blue to dark blue. The appearance of blue nevus is usually observed during puberty, but can occur at any other age (including being congenital). Multiplicity is rare. By gender, blue nevi are more often observed in women compared with men.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of blue nevi. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor: the appearance of Spitz nevus may be due to the human genome
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_1_2: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet leads to faster reproduction of nevoid cells (nevus cells) and excessive production of melanin (pigment, the accumulation of which is noted in nevus);
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_1_3: Hormonal changes: hormonal fluctuations in the body (especially sex hormones, thyroid hormones and adrenal hormones) can affect the appearance of new nevi and the growth of existing ones;
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_1_4: Ionizing radiation, viral diseases, and injuries can also provoke the appearance or growth of blue nevi.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_2_1: The diagnosis of blue nevi is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_1: On visual inspection of the blue nevus, a spot or slightly elevated nodule is determined. Most often, the formation is symmetrical (oval or round, sometimes spindle-shaped). The surface of the nevus can be a texture of ordinary skin, a smooth skin pattern (up to a glossy surface), or tuberosity (large nevi, over 10 mm in diameter).
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_3: The borders of the blue nevus are fuzzy (blurry), but usually smooth. Rarely, an uneven edge can be observed in formations with a large diameter (an unfavorable sign). The color of the blue nevus varies from blue to dark blue (including gray-blue, blue-brown shades), which is associated with a deep occurrence of pigment in the skin. In the distribution of pigment by formation, a gradual decrease in the color intensity is observed in the direction from the center to the periphery; in large nevi, there may be heterogeneity of color over the entire area, spotting (polychrome).
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_4: Hair is most often absent, sometimes can be observed on the periphery.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_5: The dimensions of the blue nevus usually do not exceed 10 mm. Growth is slow. Formations over 1 cm are very rare (blue cell nevus).
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_6: On palpation of a simple nevus, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin or somewhat denser (large, protruding forms over the skin). Subjective sensations are absent.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_3_7: Neoplasms are located mainly on the trunk, limbs, or neck, rarely on the head. Typical localization of large cell nevus is the sacro-gluteal region.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the following Spitz nevus features are visualized:
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_4_1: Star pattern: the presence of pigment strips, dots and / or globules radially diverging from the center to the periphery – the main dermatoscopic symptom
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_4_2: Symmetric blue-white structure against the background of pigmented elements (often spots) in the center of the nevus
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_4_4: Vascular network – represented by slightly curved diffuse monomorphic vessels (regular vasculature)
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_4_5: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_5_1: With dermatoscopy of the blue nevus, the following is visualized:
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_5_3: Gradual decrease in color intensity from the center to the periphery;
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_5_4: Homogeneous structureless pigmentation of a gray-blue color (a consequence of the occurrence of melanocytes in the papillary (gray) and reticular (blue) layers of the dermis);
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_5_5: Polychrome, color heterogeneity, vessels, and globules are rare signs of blue nevi.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_6_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_riks: In most cases, the blue nevus is safe. However, compared with simple pigmented nevus, the risk of melanoma on the background of blue nevus is slightly higher: less than 1% and 3%, respectively. Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the blue nevus, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, self-control (or inspection with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage to the nevus has occurred, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually) or indications are made for the removal of the damaged nevus. It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_7_4: Patients with blue nevus on the skin are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Mapping of skin neoplasms is also recommended, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or changes to existing ones.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of blue nevus using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is not recommended.
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
blue_nevus.blue_nevus_desc_9_2: A regular examination of the blue nevi, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms are also required.

Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_1: Bowen’s disease (squamous cell carcinoma of the skin in situ, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin in situ, CCM in situ) is a malignant neoplasm of the skin in the form of a hyperemic spot or plaque. Bowen’s disease is the very initial phase of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin when the cancerous growth of the basement membrane by malignant cells has not occurred. In this regard, it has a favorable prognosis and there is no likelihood of metastasis. Pathology occurs at the age of over 35-40 years, slightly more often in women.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of Bowen’s disease. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of these neoplasms:
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_1_1: Excessive insolation: excessive exposure to solar ultraviolet;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_1_3: The influence of chemical compounds that damage the skin;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_1_5: Some dermatological diseases: Mibelli’s porokeratosis, dystrophic bullous epidermolysis, lichen planus, lupus erythematosus, Lewandowski-Lutz epidermodysplasia;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_1_6: The role of human papillomavirus in increasing the risk of Bowen’s disease is not ruled out.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_2_1: The diagnosis of Bowen’s disease is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. After examination, a biopsy is performed
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_1: A visual examination of Bowen’s disease identifies single, rarely multiple, or grouped spots or plaques. The surface of the plaque differs significantly from the texture of ordinary skin: rough, tuberous, warty, focal covered with crusts, with erosion and signs of ulceration. It practically does not protrude above the skin (up to 1 mm, the edges of the tumor can protrude more).A visual examination of Bowen’s disease identifies single, rarely multiple, or grouped spots or plaques. The surface of the plaque differs significantly from the texture of ordinary skin: rough, tuberous, warty, focal covered with crusts, with erosion and signs of ulceration. It practically does not protrude above the skin (up to 1 mm, the edges of the tumor can protrude more).
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_4: The boundaries are usually clear, but uneven. The shape is irregular, asymmetric. The color is pink, pink-red, with the appearance of horny masses – gray shades join, the intensity of which depends on the severity of keratosis in the tumor area.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_5: Hair growth is absent in the focal area.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_6: Sizes range from 4 mm to 40 mm. Grouped structures from several foci can reach larger sizes. Increases slowly, grows over the years. Self-regression does not occur.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_7: On palpation, in comparison with the surrounding skin, denser formation with peeling is determined. Crusts are usually easily removed, under them is eroded skin with hyperemia. Subjective sensations are usually absent or slight itching, burning.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_3_8: The foci of Bowen’s disease are located on the torso. Also with great frequency, the face, scalp, neck, upper limbs (the area of ​​the shoulder girdle, and hand) are affected.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the following Spitz nevus features are visualized:
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_4_1: A large number of vessels in the form of glomeruli;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_4_2: Point vessels on the background of a uniform pale red or pink color;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_4_3: Uniform distribution of vascular structures throughout the formation;
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_6_1: Bowen’s disease is a non-invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the skin (cancer in situ). The main difference from conventional skin carcinoma is the absence of germination of the basement membrane, that is, the tumor is located in the uppermost layers of the epidermis. In this regard, some oncological schools treat Bowen’s disease as an obligate precancerous condition: over time, the cancer in situ necessarily transforms into an invasive form of cancer, while the tumor cells grow deeper into the skin through the basement membrane.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_6_2: Thus, Bowen’s disease itself has a favorable prognosis with timely and adequate treatment. In the absence of proper treatment and transformation into invasive cancer, the consequences can be more serious.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_7_1: The main treatment method is surgical: wide excision of the tumor focus. This is the most effective method with a low risk of local recurrence.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_7_2: Another effective and universally recognized method is short-focus x-ray therapy (radiation therapy). It is usually used to treat foci up to 20 mm.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_7_3: The use of other methods of local exposure (local chemotherapy, laser removal, or cryodestruction) is not recommended due to the high risk of relapse and the subsequent faster transformation into invasive forms of cancer.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_8_1: If you suspect or detect the first signs of Bowen’s disease, you need to consult an oncologist. The oncologist conducts additional specifying tests. In the absence of sufficient clinical data for an unambiguous diagnosis, sometimes the tactics of active dynamic observation is chosen. More often, an excision or biopsy of a suspicious lesion is performed, followed by histological examination.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_8_2: After histological confirmation of Bowen’s disease, a special treatment plan is formed.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_8_3: In this regard, patients with Bowen’s disease increase the risk of other malignant tumors – regular thorough skin examination is recommended. When suspicious neoplasms are detected, a positive role is played by their photo fixation, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance. In the same situations, an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before the beach season and after it) is indicated. Of great importance is the compilation maps of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of Bowen’s disease and its transformation into invasive forms of cancer is a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
Bowen_Disease.Bowen_Disease_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of the skin, timely consultation with a specialist in the event of external changes in skin tumors, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_1: Dysplastic nevus (atypical nevus, melanoma-dangerous nevus, Clark’s nevus) is a benign pigmented skin neoplasm with a high risk of transformation into a malignant tumor (melanoma). Dysplastic nevus (DN) can occur at any age, but the older the person, the higher the likelihood. Dysplastic nevi can be multiple, which is especially typical for people with multiple congenital nevi, as well as after excessive exposure to the skin with ultraviolet light (artificial or solar). With the same probability, they can appear in both men and women.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of dysplastic nevi. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_1_1: Genetic factor (heredity): it was found that the appearance of dysplastic nevi can be inherited in an autosomal dominant manner (dysplastic nevi syndrome). However, this is not the only reason, since Dysplastic nevi appear in people without family associations
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_1_2: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet leads to faster reproduction of nevoid cells (nevus cells), the production of melanin (pigment, the accumulation of which is noted in the nevus), and also provokes malignant degeneration
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_1_3: Hormonal changes: hormonal fluctuations in the body (especially sex hormones, thyroid hormones and adrenal hormones) can affect the appearance of new nevi and the growth of existing ones
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_1_4: Ionizing radiation and skin injuries can also provoke the appearance or growth of dysplastic nevi
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of dysplastic nevi is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_1: On visual inspection of dysplastic nevus, a spot or slightly elevated nodule is determined. Formation can be either symmetrical (oval, round, elongated), or irregular in shape. The surface of the nevus is a texture of ordinary skin, a smooth skin pattern (up to a glossy surface), small tuberosity, or peeling.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_2: The boundaries of dysplastic nevus are usually fuzzy (blurry), even. Roughness of the edge can be observed, which refers to an unfavorable sign.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_3: The color of the dysplastic nevus is very variable; there may be formations from light brown to dark brown, almost black. Often there are shades of red, pink, blue. The distribution of pigment is usually heterogeneous. This can be a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery, heterogeneity of color over the entire area, spotting (with areas up to the complete absence of pigment), the presence of several colors, or their shades (polychrome).
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_4: Hair is most often absent, or a single, sparse growth is noted.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_5: The dimensions of the dysplastic nevus usually do not exceed 10-15 mm, although larger formations (up to several centimeters) can also occur. The growth of dysplastic nevus is often slow. Rapid growth is an unfavorable sign and can mean the transformation of the nevus into melanoma.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_6: On palpation of dysplastic nevus, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin. Subjective sensations are absent, sometimes itching is present (especially after the trauma of formation, exposure to ultraviolet light).
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_3_7: There is no typical localization for dysplastic nevi; they can be located in any anatomical region.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of dysplastic nevus, the following signs are visualized:
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_4_1: Alternation of light and dark-colored areas of the pigment network
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_4_3: The presence of irregular inclusions of points and globules against the background of the pigment network
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_4_4: Globules of various shapes, sizes and colors
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_4_5: Asymmetry in color, structure and shape
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_4_9: The presence of hypopigmentation zones and structureless zones, regression structures
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_6_1: Dysplastic nevus has a high risk of transformation into melanoma, especially against the background of active ultraviolet radiation (photodamage) or chronic trauma. Signs of a possible malignancy: a change in appearance (active growth, a change in borders, pigmentation), the appearance of subjective sensations.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_1: Dysplastic nevus is often almost impossible to distinguish visually from melanoma in situ (the very initial, “zero” stage of melanoma), and therefore such formations in most cases must be removed with a mandatory histological examination.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_2: Dynamic observation is possible only if the dysplastic nevus for a long time does not show signs of activity, and only after examination by an oncologist. The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic monitoring (terms are determined individually, usually at least 1 time per month) or indications for removal are made.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_3: Removal is also necessary if there is a mechanical damage to the nevus, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, if any changes in the nevus itself are noticed or previously absent sensations appear – consultation of an oncologist.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_4: It is necessary to remove those nevi that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_5: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the nevus.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_7_6: Patients with dysplastic nevi on the skin require an oncologist examination in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Mapping of skin neoplasms is also recommended, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or changes to existing ones.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_8_1: Only surgical (classic, using an electric or radio scalpel) with a mandatory histological examination.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_8_2: Treatment of dysplastic nevi using destructive methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) is contraindicated.
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of dysplastic nevi and their malignancy consists in a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
dysplastic_nevus.dysplastic_nevus_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of all nevi, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_1: Keratoacanthoma is a benign, non-pigmented skin neoplasm with rapid growth, histological similarity to squamous cell carcinoma, and the possibility of spontaneous reverse involution several months after the appearance. Keratoacanthoma – acquired neoplasm, usually appears over the age of 35-40 years. It is more common in men than in women.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the occurrence of keratoacanthoma. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of these neoplasms:
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_1_1: Excessive insolation: excessive exposure to solar ultraviolet
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_1_3: The influence of chemical compounds that damage the skin
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of keratoacanthoma is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. Due to the external similarity with nodal forms of basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma, a biopsy is usually performed.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_1: With a visual examination of keratoacanthomas, an elevated, flattened formation is determined. The surface at the edges is smooth, the skin pattern is absent, a crust-covered indentation, or, on the contrary, a protrusion formed by excess horn masses is noted in the center. In large tumors or when the stratum corneum disappears, ulceration may be present in the center.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_2: The boundaries are usually fuzzy (although a clear border with healthy skin can sometimes be present), but they are even. The peripheral part of keratoacanthoma is usually represented by an epithelial roller. Around there may be a reaction of healthy skin in the form of hyperemia. The shape of the tumor is regular, symmetrical.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_3: Coloring on the periphery is matte pink, pink-red, yellowish shades may be present. In the center, in the presence of horny masses – gray shades. When the crusts leave, a pink-red surface with possible foci of ulceration.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_5: Sizes range from 4 mm to 40 mm. Swelling up to 20 mm is usually rapid. Above 20 mm, the keratoacanthoma grows slowly, but at this stage, soreness joins even with a slight physical impact, bleeding from the central part.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_6: On palpation, a dense, but mobile formation with respect to the subcutaneous structures is determined.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_7: Subjective sensations are usually absent. However, in formations over 15 mm there is an increased tactile sensitivity, soreness.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_3_8: Keratoacanthoma is located mainly in open areas of the body. The most favorite localization is the forearm and the back surface of the hand. It can also be found on the face, neck, back, legs, in the chest area. A little less often – the area of ​​the abdomen, hips.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy, the most reliable symptoms and signs of keratoacanthomas include:
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_1: Homogeneous pink staining on the periphery
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_2: A whitish pink or white annular peripheral region
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_3: The accumulation of keratin masses in the center surrounded by a ring-shaped roller
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_4: Inclusions in the form of small blood clots (more characteristic for the central region)
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_6: Vessels in the form of a hairpin
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_4_8: The radial orientation of the vessels.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such neoplasms as:
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_6_1: Keratoacanthoma is an optional precancerous condition. Malignancy occurs rarely and is more often observed under the influence of additional factors (chronic injury, thermal and chemical burns). In the case of malignancy, keratoacanthoma transforms more often into squamous cell (squamous) cancer.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_6_2: It should be taken into account that patients with keratoacanthoma have an increased risk of developing a malignant tumor on the unchanged skin or near the keratoacanthoma. This can complicate the timely detection and differential diagnosis of tumors.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_7_1: If keratoacanthomas are detected or suspected, an oncologist should be consulted. Due to the high degree of similarity of keratoacanthomas with basal cell carcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, a thorough differential diagnosis should be carried out, including a morphological examination after a biopsy.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_7_2: With histological confirmation of keratoacanthomas, despite the benign nature of the tumor and the possibility of its spontaneous involution, observation tactics are not recommended. This is due to the rapid growth of education, the appearance of soreness and bleeding when reaching large sizes (over 20 mm), as well as the risk of malignancy.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_7_3: In case of refusal of the patient from surgical treatment, active dynamic observation is necessary. Moreover, photographic fixation of keratoacanthomas is of great value, which will make it possible to determine even minor changes in its appearance in the future.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_7_4: Due to the increased risk of malignancy, as well as the appearance of other potentially dangerous skin neoplasms, a dermatologist or oncologist is examined in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Of great importance is the mapping of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or changes to existing ones.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_8_1: The main method of treatment is surgical: excision of keratoacanthomas with the capture of healthy skin to the entire thickness. This is the most effective method with a low risk of local recurrence.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_8_2: Excision along the plane is not recommended, since in this case, the likelihood of a reappearance of keratoacanthomas in the same place is high. Removal using local exposure methods (laser removal or cryodestruction) leads to similar consequences.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of keratoacanthomas is a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors;
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
keratoacanthoma.keratoacanthoma_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination of the skin, timely consultation with a specialist in the event of external changes in skin tumors, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

lentigo.lentigo_desc_1: Lentigo (melanin hyperpigmentation, actinic lentigo, sunspots) is a benign skin neoplasm, which is a light brown single multiform spot or a group of many smaller spots, but of the same type. Lentigo usually appears in people over 35 years old, usually under the influence of solar ultraviolet radiation. At a younger age, lentigo is rare (less than 20%), and this is more often associated with metabolic pathology or with hormonal disorders. With age, the risk of lentigo increases: in people over 60, it is found in 90% of people.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of lentigo. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of hyperpigmentation:
lentigo.lentigo_li_1_1: Ultraviolet radiation: artificial or solar ultraviolet leads to excessive production of melanin (skin pigment)
lentigo.lentigo_li_1_2: Hormonal changes: the appearance of lentigo can be affected by hormonal fluctuations in the body (especially sex hormones, thyroid hormones and adrenal hormones)
lentigo.lentigo_li_1_3: Ionizing radiation, viral diseases and injuries can also trigger the appearance or growth of lentigo
lentigo.lentigo_li_1_4: Genetic factor: the appearance of lentigo may be due to the human genome
lentigo.lentigo_li_1_5: Light skin: I-II phototype of the skin according to Fitzpatrick
lentigo.lentigo_desc_2_1: Diagnosis of lentigo is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed (excision biopsy, excision of the entire formation).
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_1: A visual examination of lentigo determines a spot or group of spots, possibly a slight elevation above the skin (usually not more than 1 mm). A neoplasm can be either symmetrical or irregular in shape (fusion of several spots, a group of separate spots, including multiple spots, occupying entire anatomical areas). The surface is a texture of ordinary skin, small tuberosity (roughness), peeling may be present.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_2: The boundaries of lentigo are clear, but most often uneven (especially large spots, multi-focal). Lentigo coloration varies from light brown to brown. Dark colors are usually absent. The distribution of pigment throughout the formation is uniform. Sometimes there is a gradual decrease in color intensity in the direction from the center to the periphery, or an irregular change of tint over the area of ​​the entire pigment focus. Over time, the color intensity may increase. Sometimes there are shades of gray as a result of keratinization of the upper layers of the epithelium.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_3: Lentigo, as a rule, does not affect hair growth.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_4: The size of the lentigo is very variable: individual spots from 2-3 mm to 3-4 cm, grouped lesions can reach several tens of centimeters.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_5: On palpation of lentigo, there are no features: the consistency of ordinary skin. Subjective sensations are also absent. In long-existing forms, roughness is noted, itching is possible.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_3_6: Lentigo is located mainly on the face or other open areas of the body. In the elderly, spots can appear on other parts of the body.
lentigo.lentigo_li_4_1: Uniform pigment network – a pattern of hypopigmented holes and uniform lines from light brown to dark brown. The lines are evenly thinning to the periphery of the formation
lentigo.lentigo_li_4_2: Pseudo-network is a reticulate structure formed by the dermal mouths and hair follicles against the background of diffuse brown pigmentation
lentigo.lentigo_li_4_3: Ring-granular structures – granular pigmentation surrounding the hair follicles in the form of a regular ring
lentigo.lentigo_li_4_4: Regular points – are small hyperpigmented round structures that are located in the center or are found on the pigmented lines of the network
lentigo.lentigo_li_4_5: Diffuse uniform staining of the entire formation
lentigo.lentigo_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such pigmented neoplasms, as:
lentigo.lentigo_desc_6_1: In the absence of external effects on lentigo (trauma, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation) – the risk of malignant degeneration of lentigo is low and almost comparable to the risk of melanoma on unchanged skin. Signs of a possible malignancy of lentigo: a change in appearance, the appearance of subjective sensations.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_6_2: Malignant lentigo (Dubreuilh melanosis) is a precancerous condition and on this background, the risk of melanoma is significantly higher.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on the lentigo, changes in appearance, and subjective sensations, self-control is sufficient at least once a year. If there is mechanical damage to the pigment spot, its active irradiation with ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes are noticed or previously absent sensations appear, you need to consult a dermatologist or oncologist.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic observation (terms are determined individually) or indications for treatment are set. It is necessary to remove those foci that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of the skin neoplasm is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in the appearance of the pigment neoplasm.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_7_4: Patients with multiple or large lesions of lentigo are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are also recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_8_1: Since lentigo is most often just a cosmetic defect, approaches, and the need for treatment are discussed individually. If the goal is not to eliminate a cosmetic defect, treatment is not required. Otherwise, small lesions may be removed surgically. Lentigo in the form of multiple of the same type of light spots can be subjected to conservative treatment in the form of various cosmetic procedures.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_8_2: Any external influences on the lentigo foci (laser treatment, cryodestruction, hardware cosmetology) should be carried out only after examination by a dermatologist or oncologist (ideally after dermatoscopy). In general, the use of destructive methods for pigment lesions is not recommended, since it is not always possible to identify the process of malignant degeneration in a timely manner and with the help of only one clinical examination.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_8_3: If surgical removal is not possible (due to the lentigo area or patient’s failure), and the elimination of a cosmetic defect becomes a priority – after the treatment, careful visual monitoring of the area where the lentigo focus was previously located is necessary.
lentigo.lentigo_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of lentigo and its malignancy is a gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
lentigo.lentigo_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
lentigo.lentigo_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
lentigo.lentigo_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
lentigo.lentigo_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
lentigo.lentigo_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors
lentigo.lentigo_desc_9_2: It also requires regular inspection of age spots, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_1: Seborrheic keratosis (seborrheic wart, senile wart, senile keratosis, senile keratoma) is a benign tumor rising above the skin with keratinization. These formations appear, as a rule, over the age of 50 years. Seborrheic keratosis is characterized by plurality, the proportion of which increases with age. Equally common in both men and women.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_1_1: There is no clear reason for the appearance of seborrheic keratosis. It is only appropriate to talk about predisposing factors that, to varying degrees, can increase the risk of neoplasms:
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_1_1: Involute (age-related) skin changes, with histological and functional changes: aging of epidermal keratinocytes with late apoptosis
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_1_3: Genetic factor: the appearance of seborrheic keratosis may be due to the human genome
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_1_4: Ionizing radiation and viral diseases can also provoke the appearance or growth of keratomas
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_2_1: The diagnosis of seborrheic keratosis is based on a clinical examination, which includes a routine examination of the formation and dermatoscopy. If you suspect malignant growth, a biopsy can be performed.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_1: A visual examination of seborrheic keratoma reveals a flattened, hemispherical, or short wide leg formation that rises above the skin, most often symmetrical (oval or round). The surface of keratoma differs significantly from the texture of ordinary skin: rough, dry, with peeling, warty (in the form of large, uneven dry papillae). Rough surfaces are more characteristic for formations over 10 mm. Sometimes keratinization is so strong that keratoma fragments can fall off on their own or with little physical impact.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_2: The boundaries of senile keratoma are clear and even. The color is nude, gray, gray-brown. Sometimes pink or pink-red shades are present. Redness of unchanged skin around the formation itself may be noted.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_3: The presence of keratoma does not affect hair growth.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_4: Sizes range from 5 mm to 20 mm. Formations over 15 mm are rare. The height of such a nevus above the skin does not exceed 5-7 mm.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_5: On palpation, a dense, dry formation with peeling is determined. Subjective sensations are usually absent or mild itching.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_3_6: Keratomas are located mainly on the trunk, upper limbs. They can be located on the face, scalp, neck, lower extremities.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_4_1: With dermatoscopy of seborrheic keratoma, the following signs are visualized:
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_1: Homogeneous background pigmentation from pale gray to brown
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_2: Comedone-like structures: clear gray-brown keratotic inclusions of the correct form
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_3: Milium-like cysts: spherical structures of a dull white color or with a yellowish tinge
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_4: Blood vessels in the form of a hairpin
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_5: Structures resembling the convolutions of the brain
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_6: Evenly colored pseudo-network with uneven, sharply breaking off edges (typical for the face)
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_4_7: Uniform dot pigmentation of gray-black color
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_5_1: Differential diagnosis is carried out with such pigmented neoplasms, as:
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_6_1: Seborrheic keratosis is an optional precancerous condition. Malignancy occurs rarely and is more often observed under the influence of additional factors (chronic injury, thermal and chemical burns). The risk of malignant transformation is 1-10%. In the case of malignancy, seborrheic keratosis is more often transformed into squamous cell (squamous) cancer. Sometimes this happens through a clinically determined phase of Bowen’s disease.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_6_2: It should be carried in mind that patients with a large number of keratomas have an increased risk of a malignant tumor on unchanged skin or near keratoma. This can complicate the timely detection and differential diagnosis of tumors.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_7_1: In the absence of any damaging effect on seborrheic keratoma, changes in appearance and subjective sensations, self-control (or examination with the help of other persons in inaccessible areas) is enough at least once a year. If mechanical damage has occurred, active exposure to ultraviolet or ionizing radiation, as well as if any changes in the keratoma itself have been noticed or previously absent sensations have appeared, a dermatologist or oncologist needs to be consulted.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_7_2: The specialist determines the possibility of further dynamic observation (terms are determined individually) or indications are set for the removal of damaged skin formation. It is necessary to remove those keratomas that are subject to constant, chronic trauma to clothing, jewelry, or due to the characteristics of professional employment.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_7_3: In the case of dynamic observation, photo fixation of skin neoplasms is of great value, which will subsequently determine even minor changes in appearance.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_7_4: Patients with seborrheic keratosis are shown an examination by a dermatologist or oncologist in the spring and autumn (before and after the beach season). Such patients are recommended to compile a map of skin neoplasms, which greatly simplifies further observation, the search for new formations, or a change in existing ones.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_8_1: Treatment can be surgical or using local destruction methods (laser, cryodestruction). After surgical treatment (classical, with the help of an electric or radio scalpel), histological examination is mandatory.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_8_2: The use of laser removal or cryodestruction is carried out after a mandatory examination by an oncologist and the exclusion of malignancy. The use of such methods is also not recommended if it is impossible to conduct a clear differential diagnosis with neoplasms of a pigmented nature (pigmented, dysplastic and other nevi).
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_9_1: Prevention of the appearance of seborrheic keratosis and its malignancy is gentle and careful attitude to the skin:
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_9_1: Limitation of ultraviolet radiation (tanning bed, solar tanning)
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_9_2: The use of protective creams during periods of active sun
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_9_4: Limitation or exclusion of ionizing radiation, occupational hazards
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_9_5: Compliance with safety measures when working with skin-damaging factors
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_li_9_6: Personal hygiene and basic awareness of skin tumors.
seborrheic_keratosis.seborrheic_keratosis_desc_9_2: It also requires regular examination by keratitis, timely consultation of a specialist in the event of external changes, and the removal of potentially dangerous neoplasms.

genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_1: Genital herpes is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). There are two different types of virus (type 1 and type 2), both of which can infect the genitals. One type (type 1) is the same virus that causes labial herpes (in the lip area). The main manifestation of genital herpes is a painful blistering rash, often with ulceration in the genital area.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_1_1: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) is easily transmitted from person to person through close, direct contact, including:
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_1_2: The infection process can occur even if the sexual partner has no visible symptoms. This is sometimes referred to as “asymptomatic discharge.”
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_1: Many people with the herpes virus do not experience any symptoms immediately after infection. The first manifestations occur approximately 2-12 days after contact. Sometimes symptoms may not be visible for months, and sometimes even several years after exposure to the virus.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_2: Once infected, the herpes virus remains in the body. It can remain dormant for a long time, but it can reactivate in the originally infected area with the onset of symptoms in the form of a painful rash. This is known as a “recurrent episode” of genital herpes.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_3: The first episode of genital herpes can last two to four weeks. If repeated episodes occur, they are usually not as severe and prolonged as the first.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_4: Symptoms of genital herpes can include patches or a red rash, often very painful, around the genitals. Over time, these spots or rashes can open up to form ulcers. The sores gradually crust over, forming new skin as it heals
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_5: Other symptoms of genital herpes include:
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_2_1: Pain in the vagina, glans penis, or rectum
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_2_3: Pain when urinating or urinary retention
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_2_5: Flu-like symptoms, back pain, headache, swollen lymph nodes in the groin
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_2_6: Recurrent genital herpes often presents with a tingling or burning sensation before the rash appears (one of the first symptoms of a recurrent infection).
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_3_1: If you suspect genital herpes, you should make an appointment with a dermatovenerologist.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_3_3: If necessary (the indications are determined by the doctor), a smear is taken for analysis to confirm the herpes infection and determine the type of herpes.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_4_1: In the case of a mild or asymptomatic course of genital herpes infection, special antiviral drugs are usually not prescribed. It is enough only for nonspecific measures that help speed up the healing process and reduce the severity of symptoms:
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_4_5: To relieve painful sensations – non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_desc_4_2: In more severe cases, antiviral drugs are prescribed on the recommendation of a doctor, which not only reduce symptoms and speed up the healing process, but also reduce the frequency of recurrent infections. The frequency and duration of admission is determined by the doctor.
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_heading_5: Preventing transmission of genital herpes to a partne
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_5_1: Inform your partner about the presence of genital herpes
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_5_2: Learn to recognize in a timely manner the precursors of the appearance of genital herpes (tingling, itching or flushing of the skin)
genital_herpes.genital_herpes_li_5_3: Exclude sexual intercourse during an episode of herpes
